question.prompt: Locations A and B are 36 km apart. Two people start simultaneously, one from each location. When traveling toward each other, they meet after 2 hours; when traveling in the same direction (with the faster person catching up from behind), the faster person catches the slower person after 6 hours. Find their speeds. (Give the faster person's speed first, then the slower person's speed, in km/h, separated by a comma.)

solutions.explanation: Let the faster person's speed be \(x\) km/h and the slower person's speed be \(y\) km/h. Meeting gives \(2(x+y)=36\), and catching up gives \(6(x-y)=36\). Thus, \(x+y=18\) and \(x-y=6\). Solving gives \(x=12\), \(y=6\).
solutions.title: Model meeting and catching up
Compute relative speeds and split them
